chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Husayn ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Hamza who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I delay the fasting of three days from each month to the winter, then I fast them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with that.'
ai.seo_question: Can I delay the three monthly fasts to winter?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) approval of postponing the voluntary monthly fasts to winter, illustrating the juristic flexibility (rukhas) in timing specific sunnah acts. It underscores that the spiritual merit of the fast remains intact regardless of seasonal adjustment, provided the intention is preserved. This ruling is often cited in Shia fiqh to demonstrate the adaptability of voluntary worship to individual circumstances and climatic conditions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Husayn Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Hamza who said,
‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I either Fast the three days from each month, or delay it to the winter, then Fast them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Husayn ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if I can delay fasting of three days of every month to fast in winter. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
